description: THE KEYSTONE PHOTOGRAPH OF THE SURVEY SO FAR. A blond U.S. soldier stands among granite boulders with his arm around the shoulders of a smiling young Vietnamese soldier who cradles a submachine gun (wooden stock, Thompson-type). The American's name tape is FULLY LEGIBLE: 'HUNNEWELL', with a 'U.S. AR[MY]' tape on the opposite chest and a large white shield-shaped patch with a dark emblem sewn or pinned at his left pocket. Behind them: sandbags stacked upper left, granite boulders bearing painted Vietnamese inscriptions in red (fragments visible: 'PHAT VAN THINH(?)', 'XY-H&N(?)', 'U-SON(?)', other lines not resolvable), and at right a dark metal equipment cabinet or shelter with heavy cables running down the rock face to it — powered equipment installed among the boulders.
visibleText: NAME TAPE: 'HUNNEWELL' — FULLY LEGIBLE. This confirms (machine-level) that the blond soldier recurring throughout the collection is Larry himself. Awaiting Larry's confirmation as a formality.
White shield-shaped pocket patch with dark emblem — MAGNIFICATION PRIORITY (unit crest candidate — direct evidence for the unit question)
Painted Vietnamese inscriptions on boulders, red paint, several lines — partially resolvable; MAGNIFICATION PRIORITY (may name the site or shrine)
